recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce the old ReferralRequest paragraph into current source; future refinements should be handled as current ServiceRequest/Appointment clarification work by the responsible work groups.
issue_request: FHIR-7670 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Patient Care change request asking for clarification between ReferralRequest and an appointment request; the accepted resolution was to state that Appointment is for booking/scheduling while ReferralRequest initiates care or transfer of care.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git commit 8feebd003a016e4f1c0b83f3f45f3776029dce83 / SVN r6679, which added a Boundaries and Relationships paragraph to source/referralrequest/referralrequest-introduction.xml saying a ReferralRequest should not be confused with Appointment because appointments are for booking/scheduling purposes.
additional_context: ReferralRequest is no longer an active current-build resource. source/fhir.ini lists ServiceRequest and Appointment as active resources and records that ReferralRequest became ServiceRequest. The old ReferralRequest introduction was later deleted with retired resource source. Current ServiceRequest narrative covers referral and transfer-of-care requests, current Appointment narrative describes booking a healthcare event, and later applied FHIR-46329 explicitly clarifies that Appointment is an intention rather than authorization and that ServiceRequest typically provides authorization when required. FHIR-47681 separately removed stale AppointmentRequest wording from Appointment recurring-appointment text.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active current source already conveys the substantive boundary requested by FHIR-7670, while the original ReferralRequest source location is obsolete/out of current build scope.

related_jiras.note: Applied Appointment narrative clarification that Appointment is an intention and ServiceRequest typically provides authorization when required.
